about.title: Architecting Sustainable,
about.subtitle: CivicReport is an open civic technology platform developed for the Smart City Exhibition 2026. It is designed to accelerate the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals by giving every resident a direct, accountable voice in their city's infrastructure.
about.sdg11Subtitle: Make cities inclusive, safe, resilient, and sustainable
about.sdg11Impact: CivicReport provides a transparent bridge between urban residents and municipal administrators, turning passive bystanders into active contributors to their local neighborhood.
about.sdg9Subtitle: Build resilient infrastructure and foster sustainable innovation
about.sdg9Impact: Utilizes modern geospatial GIS technology, WebSockets, and real-time mapping to identify critical infrastructure failure points before they lead to severe accidents.
about.sdg6Subtitle: Ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation
about.sdg6Impact: Pipeline bursts and open sewage leaks can be immediately geo-tagged by citizens, allowing water authorities to dispatch repair crews and safeguard community hygiene.
about.sdg16Subtitle: Build effective, accountable, and inclusive institutions at all levels
about.sdg16Impact: Every reported issue has a public status timeline. Municipalities cannot bury complaints, fostering public trust and institutional integrity.
about.evolutionTitle: Replacing Legacy Bureaucracy with Real-Time Action
about.comp1Legacy: Manual paper forms, lost phone calls, and unaccountable complaint boxes.
about.comp1Modern: Real-time WebSocket alerts with sub-meter GPS accuracy on an interactive GIS map.
about.comp2Legacy: Zero transparency: citizens never know if an issue is being investigated.
about.comp2Modern: Public status lifecycle: Pending → In Progress → Resolved, visible to the whole city.
about.comp3Legacy: No prioritization: urgent safety hazards sit in the same queue as minor cosmetic issues.
about.comp3Modern: Crowdsourced community upvoting automatically surfaces the most critical hazards.
about.comp4Legacy: Duplicate reports clutter staff databases and create administrative logjams.
about.comp4Modern: Proximity detection and clustered map markers prevent repetitive reports.
about.ctaHeading: Be Part of Your City's Sustainable Future

help.title: How Can We Help You?
help.subtitle: Everything you need to know about reporting civic hazards, tracking repairs, and using the smart city platform.
help.stepsSubtitle: Quick guide to lodging effective, geo-accurate complaints
help.step1Desc: Use the "Near Me" button to auto-detect your current GPS coordinates, or drag the interactive marker directly to the hazard on the map.
help.step2Desc: Take a clear, well-lit photo showing both the issue (e.g. pothole or broken streetlight) and enough surrounding context for repair crews to locate it.
help.step3Desc: Choose from Potholes, Streetlights, Garbage, Water Issue, or Other. Add a concise title and helpful notes for the municipal department.
help.step4Desc: Once submitted, your report appears instantly on the public map. Track status updates and community upvotes in your "My Reports" tab.
help.faqSubtitle: Clear answers to platform features and civic participation
help.noFaqs: No FAQs matched "{query}". Try a different keyword or contact support.
help.faq1Q: Do I need an account to view or submit civic reports?
help.faq1A: Anyone can freely browse the interactive map and community reports feed without an account. To submit new reports or access your personal "My Reports" dashboard, creating a quick free account is required to prevent fraudulent reports and verify authentic civic engagement.
help.faq2Q: How does the interactive map auto-detect my position?
help.faq2A: The platform uses the HTML5 Geolocation API with high accuracy GPS triangulation. When you click "Near Me" or open the report form, your browser requests permission to read your coordinates. Your location data is used strictly for civic issue placement.
help.faq3Q: What do the report statuses (Pending, In Progress, Resolved) mean?
help.faq3A:
• Pending: The issue has been registered and queued for municipal review.
• In Progress: The assigned department (Roads, Sanitation, Water, Lighting) has dispatched inspection or repair crews.
• Resolved: The hazard has been repaired, verified, and officially closed.
help.faq4A: Citizens can upvote any reported hazard on the map or in the reports feed. Reports with higher upvote counts signal urgent community concern, helping city administrators prioritize critical repairs first.
help.faq5Q: Why does "My Reports" require a login?
help.faq5A: Your "My Reports" dashboard is private to your authenticated session. It specifically isolates and displays the exact reports you have created, ensuring you can track personal submissions without sorting through citywide feeds.
help.faq6Q: What should I do if an issue is an immediate life-threatening emergency?
help.faq6A: CivicReport is built for municipal infrastructure maintenance and scheduled repairs. For active emergencies (such as severe electrical wire sparking, major gas leaks, collapse, or vehicle collisions), please immediately contact local emergency services (Rescue 1122 or Police 15) using the emergency hotlines listed below.
